quizzes.title: WPI Basics: Index Revision Practice
quizzes.passage:
Governments and analysts track changes in prices through a set of official price indices. The index known as WPI is treated as an important indicator of inflationary trends in the economy, and it is followed closely because it reflects price movements early in the chain of production and sale.

The Government of India has now approved a revision of the base year of this index. Along with the revised series, the government will introduce new indices for the first time. These are designed to give a more comprehensive assessment of inflation and cost pressures faced by businesses, so that pressures affecting firms are visible alongside those affecting buyers.

The index is built on the prices of goods that move between businesses and traders in large quantities. Its figures are published on a regular basis and help reveal how costs are changing across the supply network. The revision also updates the methodology, including the weights used, the treatment of missing price data, and the classification of certain commodities.

The aim of these changes is to make the index a more reliable guide to how sellers experience price movements. The revised structure is meant to reflect the present economy more accurately than the earlier series did.

questions.q: Before the revision approved by the government, the WPI was based on which base year?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the WPI base year was revised from 2011-12.

questions.q: At which point in the chain are the prices in this index recorded, relative to final consumers?
options: After goods are sold to final consumers
Only at the point of export
At the point of retail sale to households
questions.explanation: The booklet says the WPI captures prices before goods reach final consumers.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The WPI is an indicator of inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain.
Reason (R): The WPI measures retail prices paid by final consumers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The WPI does indicate chain inflation, but it measures wholesale or producer-level prices rather than retail prices.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Full form of WPI   ->   A. Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
II. Body that compiles and releases the WPI   ->   B. Production and distribution chain
III. Department under which that body works   ->   C. Wholesale Price Index
IV. Chain whose inflation trends the WPI indicates   ->   D. Office of Economic Adviser
questions.explanation: WPI stands for Wholesale Price Index, the Office of Economic Adviser compiles it, that office works under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, and it indicates trends in the production and distribution chain.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the WPI:
I. It is released by the Reserve Bank of India.
II. It captures prices after goods reach final consumers.
III. It indicates inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement III matches the booklet, since the WPI is released by the Office of Economic Adviser and captures prices before goods reach final consumers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The WPI captures prices before goods reach final consumers.
II. The base year before the revision was 2011-12.
III. The WPI is released by the Ministry of Finance.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while statement III is wrong because the Office of Economic Adviser releases the WPI.

questions.q: At which level of trade are the WPI's goods priced?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the WPI as measuring average change in prices of goods traded at wholesale or producer level.

quizzes.title: WPI Basics: Names and Figures
quizzes.passage:
Official price data help a country see how costs are moving through its economy. One important measure is an index that follows prices at an early point in the flow of goods, before the items reach ordinary buyers. Economists watch it closely because it reflects pressures that may later show up in shops and household budgets.

The government has approved a revision of the base year of this index. Along with the revised series, the government will introduce new indices for the first time. These are meant to give a broader view of price changes faced by firms that sell goods and services, including the costs they pay for inputs.

The revision also changes several technical features. The weights that give each item its importance are being rebuilt, and the method used to fill gaps in missing price data is being replaced. Some commodities are moving to different categories so that the classification reflects their role in the economy more accurately.

Taken together, the changes aim to make the index a more accurate guide to the production side of the economy, while keeping its place as a measure of price changes across the supply chain. Readers comparing the old and new figures will need to keep these differences in mind.

questions.q: Which office compiles and releases the index? (name the office)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Office of Economic Adviser compiles and releases the WPI.

questions.q: Under which department does that office function? (give the acronym)
questions.explanation: The office works under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, which is abbreviated here as DPIIT.

questions.q: What does the acronym WPI stand for? (name in full)
questions.explanation: WPI is the Wholesale Price Index, as stated in the booklet's practice questions.

questions.q: What was the index's base year before the revision? (year range)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the base year was revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23.

questions.q: What is the acronym for the new indices introduced for the first time with the revised series? (three letters)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls the new indices Producer Price Indices, abbreviated PPIs.

questions.q: Which index is described as an indicator of inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the WPI as an important indicator of inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain.

questions.q: At which trade level are the index's goods priced, before they reach final consumers? (one word)
questions.explanation: The WPI measures prices of goods traded at the wholesale or producer level before they reach final consumers.

quizzes.title: WPI and PPI: Feature Comparison Practice
quizzes.passage:
Price data in India are released through more than one index, and two of them are compared on four features: scope, focus, perspective and purpose. A feature table is a useful way to read such comparisons, because it places the two measures side by side and shows where they differ.

The Government of India has approved a revision of the base year of one index, moving it to a newer reference period. Changing the base year is a technical step, but it affects how the index is read over time, so readers who compare old and new figures should keep the change in mind.

Each index has its own design, and the feature table shows how the two differ. The table has four rows, one for each feature, and two columns, one for each measure.

Because each measure has its own design, the two should not be treated as interchangeable. A reader who checks the table can see exactly where they differ and which question each measure is built to answer. The comparison discussed here is the feature table in the booklet's current affairs summary for June 2026.

questions.q: Which index has the perspective of producer revenue and input costs?
questions.explanation: The booklet's feature table gives producer revenue and input costs as the PPI perspective.

questions.q: What is the focus of the PPI, as compared with the WPI?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the PPI focus is producer-level price changes, while the WPI focus is wholesale price movements.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The new Producer Price Indices are introduced alongside the revised WPI series.
Reason (R): The Service PPI captures inflation trends in the services sector from the producer perspective.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the Service PPI description does not explain why the new indices are introduced alongside the revised series.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Focus of the WPI   ->   A. Producer-level price changes
II. Perspective of the WPI   ->   B. Producer revenue and input costs
III. Focus of the PPI   ->   C. Market-level wholesale prices
IV. Perspective of the PPI   ->   D. Wholesale price movements
questions.explanation: The WPI focus is wholesale price movements, its perspective is market-level wholesale prices, the PPI focus is producer-level price changes, and the PPI perspective is producer revenue and input costs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Service PPI captures inflation trends in the services sector from the producer perspective.
II. The WPI's scope is primarily goods.
III. The PPI's stated purpose is inflation monitoring.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the feature table, while statement III is wrong because inflation monitoring is the stated purpose of the WPI, not the PPI.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The WPI's focus is wholesale price movements.
II. The PPI's perspective is market-level wholesale prices.
III. The new PPIs are introduced alongside the revised WPI series.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II is wrong because market-level wholesale prices is the WPI perspective.

questions.q: Which of these services is covered by the Service PPI?
questions.explanation: Railways is one of the services the booklet lists as covered by the Service PPI.

quizzes.title: WPI and PPI: Names and Phrases
quizzes.passage:
Indian price data come from more than one index, and two measures that appear together in recent reform discussions can be compared across four features. A feature table is a helpful way to read such comparisons, since it places each measure side by side and makes differences easier to see. The table has four rows, one for each feature, and two columns, one for each measure.

The four features are scope, focus, perspective and purpose. Scope refers to what the measure covers, focus refers to the kind of price movement it follows, perspective refers to the vantage point from which prices are viewed, and purpose refers to the question the measure is designed to answer.

The Government of India has approved a revision of the base year of one of these indices. Changing the base year is a technical step, but readers who compare old and new figures should keep it in mind. The revised series is to be released along with new measures that give a fuller view of price changes faced by businesses.

Because each measure has its own design, the two should not be treated as interchangeable. A reader who checks the feature table can see where they differ and which question each measure is built to answer. The comparison is taken from the booklet's current affairs summary for June 2026.

questions.q: Which index has a perspective of producer revenue and input costs? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet's feature table gives producer revenue and input costs as the perspective of the PPI.

questions.q: Name the service covered by the Service PPI that concerns rail transport. (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Railways among the services covered by the Service PPI.

questions.q: Which index has a scope that is primarily goods? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The feature table gives the WPI scope as primarily goods, while the PPI scope covers goods and services.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the PPI in the comparison? (name the phrase)
questions.explanation: The feature table gives comprehensive producer inflation analysis as the PPI purpose, while the WPI purpose is inflation monitoring.

questions.q: What is the stated focus of the PPI? (name the phrase)
questions.explanation: The feature table gives producer-level price changes as the PPI focus.

questions.q: What is the stated focus of the WPI? (name the phrase)
questions.explanation: The feature table gives wholesale price movements as the WPI focus.

questions.q: Which PPI covers inflation trends in the services sector from the producer perspective? (name the PPI)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Service PPI captures inflation trends in the services sector from the producer perspective.
